"Implement the solution in src/main/java/QueenAttackCalculator.java, src/main/java/Queen.java so that the tests in src/test/java/QueenAttackCalculatorTest.java pass. The specification follows.

# Instructions

Given the position of two queens on a chess board, indicate whether or not they are positioned so that they can attack each other.

In the game of chess, a queen can attack pieces which are on the same row, column, or diagonal.

A chessboard can be represented by an 8 by 8 array.

So if you are told the white queen is at `c5` (zero-indexed at column 2, row 3) and the black queen at `f2` (zero-indexed at column 5, row 6), then you know that the set-up is like so:

![A chess board with two queens. Arrows emanating from the queen at c5 indicate possible directions of capture along file, rank and diagonal.](https://assets.exercism.org/images/exercises/queen-attack/queen-capture.svg)

You are also able to answer whether the queens can attack each other.
In this case, that answer would be yes, they can, because both pieces share a diagonal.

## Credit

The chessboard image was made by [habere-et-dispertire][habere-et-dispertire] using LaTeX and the [chessboard package][chessboard-package] by Ulrike Fischer.

[habere-et-dispertire]: https://exercism.org/profiles/habere-et-dispertire
[chessboard-package]: https://github.com/u-fischer/chessboard


Do NOT modify the tests or the build files except as stated below. Do not create new files unless the specification requires them; Helper classes may go only in the solution's package."

Now I understand the requirements. Let me implement the two classes.

For `Queen.java`:
- Constructor takes `row` and `column`.
- Validate: row must be positive (>= 0), message "Queen position must have positive row."
- row must be <= 7, message "Queen position must have row <= 7."
- column must be positive (>= 0), message "Queen position must have positive column."
- column must be <= 7, message "Queen position must have column <= 7."

For `QueenAttackCalculator.java`:
- Constructor takes two Queens.
- If either is null, throw IllegalArgumentException "You must supply valid positions for both Queens."
- If both occupy the same square, throw IllegalArgumentException "Queens cannot occupy the same position."
- `canQueensAttackOneAnother()` returns true if same row, same column, or diagonal.

Let me write the code.
Both files are stubs and the test defines the exact contract. Let me implement them.

All 15 tests passed. The implementation is complete. Let me give a brief summary.

All 15 tests pass. Here's what I implemented:

**`src/main/java/Queen.java`** — stores `row` and `column` as final fields and validates the position in the constructor, throwing `IllegalArgumentException` with the exact messages the tests expect:
- `row < 0` → "Queen position must have positive row."
- `row > 7` → "Queen position must have row <= 7."
- `column < 0` → "Queen position must have positive column."
- `column > 7` → "Queen position must have column <= 7."

**`src/main/java/QueenAttackCalculator.java`** — the constructor rejects a `null` queen ("You must supply valid positions for both Queens.") and two queens on the same square ("Queens cannot occupy the same position."). `canQueensAttackOneAnother()` returns true when the queens share a row, a column, or a diagonal — the diagonal check is `|rowDistance| == |columnDistance|`, which correctly handles both diagonal directions.

No test or build files were modified, and no new files were created.
